key_insight: A two-level machine-learning framework can efficiently map thermodynamic stability across complex hybrid perovskite alloy compositions and reveals that stable regions are narrower in Sn-based systems than in Pb-based ones.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route for screening compositionally disordered perovskites and narrowing candidate formulations for more stable solar-cell materials.
method: Graph neural network interatomic potentials trained on DFT data enabled fast structure relaxations.
A secondary ML model predicted energies directly from unrelaxed alloy structures.
Free-energy landscapes were computed across composition and phase space while accounting for alloy disorder and FA orientations.
evidence_signal: The models were used to evaluate free-energy landscapes for (Cs/FA)Pb(Br/I)3 and (Cs/FA)Sn(Br/I)3, showing maximum stability at high iodide content and no stabilization near the center of composition space.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the quality and coverage of the DFT training data, so extrapolation to unseen chemistries or extreme compositions may be unreliable.
paper_title: Charting the thermodynamic stability of hybrid perovskite alloys with machine learning
